title: Launch plan: Status page transparency upgrades (comms, training, phased rollout, audits)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Deliver a low-risk, phased rollout of Status Page Transparency Upgrades that improves (a) component granularity, (b) speed + consistency of incident updates, and (c) publishable post-incident summaries—without increasing on-call burden or over-promising SLAs.

Scope of this ticket
This is the cross-functional LAUNCH PLAN + enablement + audit schedule. It is not the component taxonomy itself, the incident-bot implementation, or the dashboards (tracked in ENG/DES tickets).

Launch principles
- Default to clarity and accuracy over completeness (especially early in incident lifecycle).
- Keep customer-facing language general; avoid customer-specific capacity details.
- Reduce cognitive load on on-call: templates + automation + explicit roles/approval chain.
- Ship in phases with measured success criteria; rollback by disabling automation / hiding new components if needed.

Success metrics (launch + 30 days)
- TTFU (time-to-first-update on status page):
  - Sev0/Sev1: first public update within 15 minutes (target), 30 minutes (max) barring legal/security constraints.
  - Sev2: within 45 minutes.
- Accuracy: <5% of incidents with component/region mismatch between internal incident tags and status page updates (measured by weekly audit job).
- Support ticket deflection: reduction in “status page inaccurate / too coarse” tickets vs baseline (Support to provide weekly counts).
- Post-incident summaries: published within 5 business days for Sev0/Sev1 (policy in PM-612), with consistent format and no confidentiality leaks.

Phased rollout plan
Phase 0 — Internal readiness (Dogfood)
Owner: Rafael Mendes (SRE delivery) + Paula Mendes (PM) + Allison Grant (observability)
Exit criteria:
- Component registry validated in staging; naming matches taxonomy and dashboards.
- Incident-bot intake requires component/region/capability fields for Sev0/Sev1.
- Templates available in runbook + incident-bot draft generation.
- Support/CS macros updated (tracked via INT-10430).
- Training sessions delivered (see below).

Phase 1 — Limited public rollout (1–2 regions or selected component groups)
Recommendation: start with Hosted API + Streaming for US-East and EU-West (highest ticket volume + clearest customer pain).
Guardrails:
- Automation enabled in “draft-only” mode for the first week (incident-bot generates text, Comms Lead posts manually).
- Anti-flap logic enabled; any repeated flapping triggers automatic revert to “manual only” until tuned.
Exit criteria:
- At least 2 drills/game-days and 1 real incident (if it occurs) completed with updated process.
- Audit shows component mapping accuracy >= 95% for week.

Phase 2 — Full public rollout
Expand to remaining Hosted components (Embeddings, Reranking) and additional regions; add Dedicated control-plane signals as defined in taxonomy/policy.
Note: Private/VPC/on-prem incidents remain governed by PM-612 policy (status page may show “Platform / Control Plane” impact where applicable without customer identification).

Comms plan (internal + external)
Internal announcements
- #announcements: 1 launch announcement + 1 reminder the day before turning on Phase 1.
- #eng-oncall + #incidents: pinned quick links (taxonomy, runbook, templates, dashboards).
- Support/CS: send a short “what changed / how to use” note and confirm macro availability.
Draft internal announcement (for #announcements)
Title: “Status Page v2: new components + faster incident updates (phased rollout)”
Body:
- What’s changing: new component breakdown by product surface + region; new standard incident update templates; Comms Lead role now required for Sev0/Sev1.
- What you need to do: tag incidents with component/region/capability in incident-bot; follow the status page update runbook; use templates (don’t improvise under pressure).
- Where to find docs: links to runbook, templates, component taxonomy, dashboards.
- Rollout schedule: Phase 0 internal → Phase 1 limited public → Phase 2 full.

External/customer-facing comms
- Status page itself: we will not post a “marketing” announcement; changes are reflected via component layout and improved incident updates.
- Docs: publish a short customer-facing explainer (“How to interpret components + incident updates”), linking to post-incident summaries format (tracked in docs PRs / redwood-docs).
- Account comms: CS can proactively share the new post-incident summary format with top escalators/prospects (Northbridge, Lattice Financial) after Phase 1 stability.

Training & enablement (required)
Audience: Incident Commanders, Comms Leads, Scribes, Support escalation responders.
Format: 30 min training + 15 min Q&A; recorded.
Sessions (proposed)
1) “Status page updates 101 (Comms Lead)”
- Owner: Rafael Mendes + Wei Chen
- Covers: what to post in Investigating/Identified/Mitigating/Monitoring/Resolved; what not to say; approval flow for Sev0/Sev1.
2) “Component taxonomy + choosing impacted components/regions”
- Owner: Mina Haddad + Ravi Menon
- Covers: common edge cases (partial region, streaming-only failures, latency-only degradation), mapping rules.
3) “Support/CS workflow: disputes + escalation path”
- Owner: Dev Patel + Jasmine Liu
- Covers: escalation playbook, evidence collection, customer response macros.

Training completion requirement
- For Phase 1: at least 80% of current IC rotation + 100% of Comms Lead rotation trained OR received the recording + short quiz confirmation.
- For new on-call joiners: add to onboarding checklist (SRE to update on-call onboarding doc; track separately).

Post-launch audit schedule (first 6 weeks)
Weekly (SRE/PM)
- Status accuracy audit review (mismatch patterns, mapping regressions).
- TTFU report (Sev0/1/2) + “template adherence” spot checks.
- Support ticket trend review: count + common complaints.
- Anti-flap tuning review: any components toggling excessively.
Bi-weekly (cross-functional)
- Review post-incident summaries published: time-to-publish, redactions needed, legal/security issues.
- Review customer feedback: top accounts + prospects.
30-day review / decision point
- Decide if we:
  - Expand components further (e.g., capability split within Hosted API),
  - Adjust thresholds for degraded performance vs partial outage,
  - Enable more automation (auto-publish with approval for Sev0/1),
  - Update support macros and customer docs.

Launch checklist (go/no-go)
Go criteria for Phase 1
- Component registry schema passes validation; components visible on status page staging.
- Dashboards available per component/region with links in runbook.
- Incident-bot draft generation works end-to-end; paging/ownership correct.
- Approval workflow defined for Sev0/Sev1 (Support lead or IC signoff as per policy).
- Training completed (see requirement).
- Rollback plan reviewed.

Rollback plan
- Primary: toggle incident-bot integration to “draft-only” (no auto-publish) and revert to previous component grouping if severe confusion occurs.
- Secondary: hide new components behind rollout flag; collapse to top-level product components until mapping issues resolved.
- Comms: if rollback occurs, post a short internal note; do not post external explanation unless customer-facing behavior materially changes.

Open questions to resolve before Phase 1
- Dedicated/Private boundary cases: when do we reflect control-plane vs customer-isolated capacity issues publicly? (confirm final language with Kira Thompson + Michael Grant).
- Latency-only degradations: confirm thresholds and whether they trigger “Degraded Performance” status (align with observability standards).
- Ownership for ongoing component taxonomy changes: who approves registry PRs and how quickly? (tie to ADR for source-of-truth + review requirements).
